target.name: Interleukin-2 signaling
target.description: Interleukin-2 signaling is the growth and survival input that antigen-stimulated T cells use to expand, and the same input that keeps the immune system from turning on itself. Originally named T cell growth factor, IL-2 also sensitizes activated T cells to activation-induced cell death and sustains regulatory T cells, so loss of the cytokine or its receptor produces lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity rather than simple immunodeficiency.

target.name: Defective SLC22A12 causes renal hypouricemia 1 (RHUC1)
target.description: Blood urate levels are set largely in the kidney, where most filtered urate is recovered rather than excreted, and URAT1 encoded by SLC22A12 is the apical exchanger in proximal tubule cells that performs that reabsorption, swapping urate for intracellular organic anions such as lactate. Loss-of-function mutations cause renal hypouricemia type 1, in which urate escapes into the urine, serum urate falls to very low levels, and patients are prone to exercise-induced acute kidney injury and urolithiasis.
